## Cleaning data

This is a continuation from importing data.\
\
***Variable naming convention used are :***\
data : main dataframe\
parameter : IMPC parameter data frame\
procedure : IMPC procedure data frame\
disease : Disease information data frame

***Steps***

Main data cleaning :\
1. correct any eronous data format on each data column\
2. correct appropriate duplicates\
3. visualize missing data\
4. handle missing data\
5. change column classes and save cleaned files

Data cleaning for parameter\
Data cleaning for procedure\
Data cleaning for disease

Loading Packages

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
```

Importing env

```{r}
load("./precleaned.RData")
```

Assign variable conventions

```{r}
data <- precleaned_data
parameter <- precleaned_parameter
procedure <- precleaned_procedure
disease <- precleaned_disease
bespoke <- precleaned_bespoke
```

## Data Cleaning -Main Data

### 1. Correct erronous data format

*refer to SOP for expected values or data format*

analysis_id (Ying qi) Found 2 missing analysis_id values and no format or filename mismatches. Duplicate entries were retained for later review.

```{r}
#there should be no typos in analysis_id
sum(is.na(data$analysis_id))
sum(duplicated(data$analysis_id[!is.na(data$analysis_id)]))
data %>%
  filter(is.na(analysis_id)) %>%
  select(file, analysis_id)

data %>%
  filter(!is.na(analysis_id)) %>%
  add_count(analysis_id, name = "n") %>%
  filter(n > 1) %>%
  select(file, analysis_id, n) %>%
  arrange(analysis_id, file) %>%
  View()

dup_rows <- data %>%
  filter(!is.na(analysis_id)) %>%
  add_count(analysis_id, name = "n") %>%
  filter(n > 1)

sum(duplicated(dup_rows %>% select(-file, -n)))


duplicate_status <- dup_rows %>%
  group_by(analysis_id) %>%
  summarise(
    different_records = nrow(distinct(pick(-file, -n))),
    files = paste(file, collapse = ", "),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(different_records > 1)

View(duplicate_status)

different_values <- dup_rows %>%
  select(-n) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -c(file, analysis_id),
    names_to = "column",
    values_to = "value"
  ) %>%
  group_by(analysis_id, column) %>%
  filter(n_distinct(value) > 1) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  arrange(analysis_id, column, file)

View(different_values)


library(stringr)

analysis_id_format_check <- data %>%
  filter(!is.na(analysis_id)) %>%
  mutate(
    id_trim = str_trim(analysis_id),
    format_ok = str_detect(id_trim, "^an[0-9]+$")
  ) %>%
  filter(analysis_id != id_trim | !format_ok) %>%
  select(file, analysis_id, id_trim, format_ok) %>%
  distinct()

analysis_id_format_check %>% count(format_ok)
View(analysis_id_format_check)


library(stringr)
library(dplyr)

analysis_id_spelling_check <- data %>%
  filter(!is.na(analysis_id)) %>%
  mutate(
    id_from_file = stringr::str_remove(
      file, "(_[0-9]+)?\\.csv$"
    ),
    spelling_check = case_when(
      analysis_id == id_from_file ~ "match",
      tolower(analysis_id) == tolower(id_from_file) ~ "case_difference",
      TRUE ~ "does_not_match_file"
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(spelling_check != "match") %>%
  select(file, analysis_id, id_from_file, spelling_check) %>%
  distinct()

analysis_id_spelling_check %>% count(spelling_check)
View(analysis_id_spelling_check)
```

gene_accession_id (Musa)

No missing values or formatting errors were found. All 2,846 unique IDs follow the expected MGI format, so no corrections are needed. The 1,924 IDs absent from the disease reference are retained because that reference is not a complete gene database.

```{r}
#checking missing gene IDs
sum(is.na(data$gene_accession_id))

#checking unexpected ID format
sum(!grepl("^MGI:[0-9]+$", data$gene_accession_id))

#checking unique gene IDs
length(unique(data$gene_accession_id))

#checking IDs against disease reference
length(setdiff(unique(data$gene_accession_id), disease$mgi_id))

#no corrections needed
```

gene_symbol (Ying qi) Corrected three gene symbols using gene_accession_id: Map2k2, Spata24, and Got1. Preserved the original values in gene_symbol_original.

```{r}
library(dplyr)

if (!"gene_symbol_original" %in% names(data)) {
  data$gene_symbol_original <- data$gene_symbol
}

data <- data %>%
  mutate(
    gene_symbol = case_when(
      gene_accession_id == "MGI:1346867" ~ "Map2k2",
      gene_accession_id == "MGI:1918492" ~ "Spata24",
      gene_accession_id == "MGI:95791"   ~ "Got1",
      TRUE ~ gene_symbol
    )
  )

data %>%
  filter(gene_accession_id %in%
           c("MGI:1346867", "MGI:1918492", "MGI:95791")) %>%
  distinct(gene_accession_id, gene_symbol_original, gene_symbol)
write.csv(data, "gene_symbol_corrected.csv", row.names = FALSE, na = "")
save(data, file = "gene_symbol_corrected.RData")
```

parameter_id (Musa)\
Found 278 missing values and many formatting inconsistencies. The code below preserves the original IDs, identifies candidates, and corrects those supported by the parameter reference or repeated matching records in the main data and values that cannot be confidently matched remains unchanged

```{r}
#save original values
if (!"parameter_stable_id_original" %in% names(data)) {
  data$parameter_stable_id_original <- data$parameter_stable_id
}

#checking missing IDs
sum(is.na(data$parameter_stable_id))

#checking unexpected characters
sum(!is.na(data$parameter_stable_id) &
      grepl("[^A-Za-z0-9_-]", data$parameter_stable_id))

#reference IDs and existing valid IDs
parameter_lookup <- bind_rows(
  parameter %>%
    transmute(
      correct_id = parameterId,
      reference_name = param_name,
      priority = 1
    ),
  data %>%
    filter(
      !is.na(parameter_stable_id),
      grepl(
        "^[A-Z]+(-[A-Z]+)*_[A-Z0-9]+_[0-9]{3}_[0-9]{3}(_[0-9]{3})?$",
        parameter_stable_id
      )
    ) %>%
    count(parameter_stable_id, parameter_name, name = "n") %>%
    filter(n >= 2) %>%
    transmute(
      correct_id = parameter_stable_id,
      reference_name = parameter_name,
      priority = 2
    )
) %>%
  filter(!is.na(correct_id), !is.na(reference_name)) %>%
  mutate(
    id_key = toupper(correct_id),
    name_key = tolower(trimws(reference_name))
  ) %>%
  arrange(priority) %>%
  group_by(id_key, name_key) %>%
  summarise(correct_id = first(correct_id), .groups = "drop")

#find possible corrections
parameter_corrections <- data %>%
  mutate(
    row_index = row_number(),
    candidate_key = toupper(
      gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9_-]", "", parameter_stable_id)
    ),
    name_key = tolower(trimws(parameter_name))
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    parameter_lookup,
    by = c("candidate_key" = "id_key", "name_key")
  ) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(parameter_stable_id),
    !is.na(correct_id),
    parameter_stable_id != correct_id
  )

#correct IDs with matching reference or existing values
data$parameter_stable_id[parameter_corrections$row_index] <-
  parameter_corrections$correct_id

#correct additional examples supported by earlier checks
data <- data %>%
  mutate(
    parameter_stable_id = case_when(
      parameter_stable_id_original == "!IMP-C_GEM_021_001" &
        parameter_name == "Ear Morphology" ~ "IMPC_GEM_021_001",
      
      parameter_stable_id_original == "&IM-PC_OFD_011_001" &
        parameter_name == "Periphery resting time" ~ "IMPC_OFD_011_001",
      
      parameter_stable_id_original == "-IM)PC_CBC_007_001" &
        parameter_name == "Albumin" ~ "IMPC_CBC_007_001",
      
      parameter_stable_id_original == "IMPC_C-SD_0#12_0-01" &
        parameter_name == "Coat - hair distribution - head" ~
        "IMPC_CSD_012_001",
      
      parameter_stable_id_original == "UCD_O_WT_01.2_00(1" &
        parameter_name == "Right lung weight" ~ "UCD_OWT_012_001",
      
      TRUE ~ parameter_stable_id
    )
  )

#checking corrections
sum(data$parameter_stable_id !=
      data$parameter_stable_id_original, na.rm = TRUE)

#checking remaining missing values
sum(is.na(data$parameter_stable_id))

#checking remaining unexpected characters
sum(!is.na(data$parameter_stable_id) &
      grepl("[^A-Za-z0-9_-]", data$parameter_stable_id))
```

parameter_name (Ying qi) All 18,150 parameter names with matching reference IDs were exact matches. The other 9,505 records had no reference ID and could not be checked. No differences were found, and no names were changed.

```{r}
library(dplyr)

parameter_lookup <- parameter %>%
  distinct(parameterId, param_name) %>%
  group_by(parameterId) %>%
  filter(n_distinct(param_name) == 1) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  distinct(parameterId, .keep_all = TRUE)

parameter_name_check <- data %>%
  left_join(
    parameter_lookup,
    by = c("parameter_stable_id" = "parameterId")
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    name_check = case_when(
      is.na(param_name) ~ "no_reference",
      is.na(parameter_name) ~ "missing_in_data",
      parameter_name == param_name ~ "match",
      TRUE ~ "mismatch"
    )
  )

parameter_name_check %>%
  count(name_check)

parameter_name_check %>%
  filter(name_check != "match") %>%
  select(file, parameter_stable_id, parameter_name, param_name, name_check) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  View()



parameter_name_check <- parameter_name_check %>%
  mutate(
    name_check_detail = case_when(
      is.na(param_name) ~ "no_reference",
      is.na(parameter_name) ~ "missing_in_data",
      parameter_name == param_name ~ "exact_match",
      tolower(trimws(parameter_name)) ==
        tolower(trimws(param_name)) ~ "case_or_outer_space_difference",
      TRUE ~ "other_difference"
    )
  )

parameter_name_check %>%
  count(name_check_detail)

parameter_name_check %>%
  filter(name_check_detail %in%
           c("case_or_outer_space_difference", "other_difference")) %>%
  select(file, parameter_stable_id, parameter_name, param_name,
         name_check_detail) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  View()
```

p_value (Rexel)

- 1 row has value 1.1. Changed to NA
- Many pvalue is 0. Assume its because its so small, need to floor it before log transformation later

```{r}
#convert to number
data$p_value <- as.numeric(data$p_value)

#checking unexpected value 
pvalue_check <- data %>% 
  filter(p_value <=0 | p_value >1 | is.na(p_value))
View(pvalue_check)

unique(pvalue_check$p_value) #spotted eronous p value of 1.1
which(data$p_value == 1.1) 
#convert pvalue of 1.1 to NA 
data$p_value[data$p_value == 1.1] <-  NA

#there are many p value with 0, possibly due to rounding errors
#we need to floor them later when doing analysis
```

allele_symbol (musa)

Found 270 missing values, one incomplete angle-bracket symbol and multiple formatting inconsistencies. The code below uses existing well-formed allele symbols for the same gene accession ID and strain, while preserving allele variants such as "tm1a" and "tm1b".

This corrects supported formatting variations but deliberately leaves incomplete symbols such as `Wnt11<`, ambiguous matches and missing alleles for further review.

```{r}
#save original values
if (!"allele_symbol_original" %in% names(data)) {
  data$allele_symbol_original <- data$allele_symbol
}

#checking missing allele symbols
sum(is.na(data$allele_symbol))

#checking unique allele symbols
n_distinct(data$allele_symbol, na.rm = TRUE)

#find repeated, well-formed allele symbols
allele_lookup <- data %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(allele_symbol),
    grepl(
      "^[A-Za-z0-9]+<[^()<>]+\\([^()<>]+\\)[^()<>]+>$",
      allele_symbol
    ),
    !grepl("[!@#$%^&*+_]", allele_symbol)
  ) %>%
  count(gene_accession_id, strain_name, allele_symbol, name = "n") %>%
  filter(n >= 2) %>%
  mutate(allele_key = toupper(allele_symbol)) %>%
  group_by(gene_accession_id, strain_name, allele_key) %>%
  slice_max(n, n = 1, with_ties = TRUE) %>%
  filter(n() == 1) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  transmute(
    gene_accession_id,
    strain_name,
    allele_key,
    correct_allele = allele_symbol
  )

#find possible allele corrections
allele_corrections <- data %>%
  mutate(
    row_index = row_number(),
    candidate_allele = gsub("[!@#$%^&*+_]", "", allele_symbol),
    allele_gene = sub("<.*$", "", candidate_allele),
    candidate_allele = if_else(
      !is.na(gene_symbol) &
        grepl("^[A-Za-z0-9]+$", gene_symbol) &
        tolower(gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]", "", allele_gene)) ==
        tolower(gene_symbol) &
        grepl("<", candidate_allele, fixed = TRUE),
      paste0(gene_symbol, sub("^[^<]*", "", candidate_allele)),
      candidate_allele
    ),
    allele_key = toupper(candidate_allele)
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    allele_lookup,
    by = c("gene_accession_id", "strain_name", "allele_key")
  ) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(allele_symbol),
    !is.na(correct_allele),
    allele_symbol != correct_allele
  )

#correct alleles with an existing matching value
data$allele_symbol[allele_corrections$row_index] <-
  allele_corrections$correct_allele

#correct additional examples supported by earlier checks
data <- data %>%
  mutate(
    allele_symbol = case_when(
      gene_accession_id == "MGI:101948" &
        allele_symbol_original == "Wnt11<tm1-.1(KOMP)Vlcg>" ~
        "Wnt11<tm1.1(KOMP)Vlcg>",
      
      gene_accession_id == "MGI:1336167" &
        allele_symbol_original == "Prkab11<tm1b(KOMP)Wt(si>" ~
        "Prkab1<tm1b(KOMP)Wtsi>",
      
      gene_accession_id == "MGI:1913955" &
        allele_symbol_original == "Dnase1l2<tm1).1(KOMP)#Wtsi>" ~
        "Dnase1l2<tm1.1(KOMP)Wtsi>",
      
      TRUE ~ allele_symbol
    )
  )

#checking number of corrections
sum(data$allele_symbol !=
      data$allele_symbol_original, na.rm = TRUE)

#checking remaining missing values
sum(is.na(data$allele_symbol))

#checking remaining unbalanced parentheses
sum(
  stringr::str_count(data$allele_symbol, fixed("(")) !=
    stringr::str_count(data$allele_symbol, fixed(")")),
  na.rm = TRUE
)

#checking incomplete angle brackets
sum(
  !is.na(data$allele_symbol) &
    (!grepl("<", data$allele_symbol, fixed = TRUE) |
       !grepl(">", data$allele_symbol, fixed = TRUE))
)
```

lacz\_ (tom)

- 663 typos corrected in lacz_blood, 504 in brain, 575 in colon, 588 in eye, 908 in heart. 604 in kidney, 640 in liver, 600 in lung, 941 in skeletal muscle, 595 in skin, 953 in vascular system.

```{r}
correct_vals <- c("expression", "NA", "no expression", "tissue not available")
# Didn't set the loop here, just change the lacz_* below to the one you want to check
unique_vals <- unique(data$lacz_vascular_system)
suggested_corrections <- data.frame(
  original = unique_vals,
  suggested = correct_vals[
    amatch(unique_vals, correct_vals, maxDist = 3)
  ]
)
print(suggested_corrections)
lacz <- c("lacz_blood", "lacz_brain", "lacz_colon", "lacz_eye", "lacz_heart", "lacz_kidney", "lacz_liver", 
          "lacz_lung", "lacz_skeletal_muscle", "lacz_skin", "lacz_vascular_system")

for (col in lacz){
  data[[col]] <- correct_vals[
    amatch(data[[col]],
           correct_vals,
           maxDist = 3)
  ]
}
```

### 2. Correct appropriate duplicates

I tried to analyse if analysis_id is unique and find that there is duplicated files that ends with \_1.csv. I will adjust and do additional cross checking after we have corrected all typos

***dont run this code yet***

```{r}
##analysis_id
#check for duplicates
dim(data)
sum(duplicated(data$analysis_id))

dup_id <- data[data$analysis_id %in% data$analysis_id[duplicated(data$analysis_id)],]
dim(dup_id)
View(dup_id)

#id duplicates seems to come from files that ends with _1.csv
#check the number of _1.csv files
sum(grepl("_1.csv$", data$file)) #69 
sum(is.na(data$analysis_id)) #2
#this confirms that id duplicates comes from duplicated file and 2 NAs

#remove duplicates except the NAs
data <- data %>%
  filter(is.na(analysis_id) | !duplicated(analysis_id))
dim(data) 
#27655 - 27586 = 71
#removes 69 "_1.csv" duplicates
# + retain 2 rows with NAs for further analysis
```

## Data Cleaning - Procedure (Yingqi)

Checked for missing proc_desc values, exact duplicate rows, and inconsistent capitalisation in proc_name. Found 3,481 missing descriptions and no exact duplicates. The two ECG descriptions belong to different ID groups; no corrections were needed.

```{r}
procedure_case_check <- procedure %>%
  filter(!is.na(proc_name), trimws(proc_name) != "") %>%
  mutate(name_lower = tolower(trimws(proc_name))) %>%
  group_by(name_lower) %>%
  filter(n_distinct(trimws(proc_name)) > 1) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(proc_name, proc_desc, impcParameterOrigId) %>%
  distinct()

View(procedure_case_check)
```
